title: Top pay at benefit districts against organizations of like size
question: Is the highest-paid person at each district paid more than the highest-paid person at City-funded organizations with a similar budget?
finding: Of 12 district organizations that can be compared, 1 pays the highest-paid person one and a half times the middle figure for organizations of like size or more: Union Square Business Improvmnt District (Marisa Rodriguez, CEO, $394,479; 1.72 times). The middle district pays 0.93 times its peers: nothing unusual on the whole. The highest figure is $394,479. 2 district organizations list no officer or key employee paid by the organization itself in the latest return.
how: From the latest return of each district organization: the largest total (reportable pay plus other compensation) among the officers, directors and key employees it lists, set against the middle such figure among the other City-funded organizations on file whose total expenses in their latest return are between half and twice the district’s. A comparison is made only where at least eight such organizations exist. Officers are named with their pay as the public return names them.
limits: A district’s budget understates the job: a chief executive answers to a board of property owners and runs cleaning and safety crews that are mostly contracted out, so a small payroll can sit under a large programme. Peers here are service nonprofits of every kind, not other downtown management bodies, and pay in a single year can include a payout on leaving. Pay set by a private board from private assessments is that board’s decision; it becomes a public question only to the extent City grants fund it. What would settle that: the grant budgets, which show whether City money pays any part of the salary.
